overview.text: Dubai, often referred to as the “City of Gold” or the “Pearl of the Gulf,” is a captivating and dynamic metropolis located in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Nestled on the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, Dubai has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past few decades, evolving from a small fishing village into a global hub for finance, tourism, and innovation. One of Dubai’s most iconic features is its stunning skyline, dominated by awe-inspiring skyscrapers such as the Burj Khalifa, the world’s tallest building. This architectural marvel is a testament to Dubai’s ambition and commitment to pushing the boundaries of what is possible. It serves as a symbol of the city’s determination to be at the forefront of modernity and innovation. Dubai’s economic prosperity is underpinned by its strategic location as a major global business and transportation hub. The city’s state-of-the-art ports and airports facilitate trade and commerce, making it a vital link in the global supply chain. Additionally, Dubai has positioned itself as a tax-free haven, attracting businesses and investors from around the world. Tourism plays a significant role in Dubai’s economy, with millions of visitors flocking to the city each year. Dubai offers an array of attractions, from luxurious resorts and pristine beaches to world-class shopping and entertainment options. The Palm Jumeirah, an artificial island shaped like a palm tree, and the Dubai Mall, one of the largest shopping malls on the planet, are just a few of the must-see destinations. Dubai’s commitment to innovation and technology is evident in projects like the Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, which have fostered a thriving tech and media sector. Moreover, the city’s dedication to sustainability is reflected in initiatives like the Dubai Expo 2020, which showcased cutting-edge sustainable technologies and solutions to address global challenges. The cultural diversity in Dubai is a reflection of its open and inclusive society. The city is home to people from all corners of the world, creating a rich tapestry of cultures, languages, and traditions. Dubai’s commitment to tolerance and coexistence has made it a model for multiculturalism in the Middle East. Dubai also boasts a thriving arts and cultural scene, with world-class museums, galleries, and theaters. The Dubai Opera House, for example, hosts a wide range of international performances, from classical music to contemporary theater. In terms of lifestyle, Dubai offers an unparalleled blend of modernity and tradition. While it embraces all the conveniences of a cosmopolitan city, it also respects its heritage and traditions, evident in places like the historic Al Fahidi District and the bustling souks where traditional crafts and spices are sold. In conclusion, Dubai stands as a testament to human ambition and innovation. This city in the desert has defied the odds, transforming itself into a global powerhouse known for its striking architecture, economic prowess, and cultural vibrancy. It continues to be a place where dreams are turned into reality, attracting people from all walks of life who seek to be part of its incredible journey of growth and development.

The capital of United Arab Emirates, Abu Dhabi is also the second most populated city in UAE. Here you can see amazing sights like the largest hand-loomed carpet in the world, a falcon hospital, man-made islands, the skyscraper with the greatest lean, the biggest sand dunes, the fastest roller coaster and much more. The city is just 1.5 hours away from exciting Dubai but is laid back and peaceful with more parks, tree-lined streets, and wider roads. Though it has more of an authentic Arabian ambiance, rapid urbanization and development have turned it into one of the richest cities in the world. Abu Dhabi now plays host to tourists who come from all corners of the globe to witness this rich culture which is unspoiled by the intoxication of most tourist destinations. A visit to Abu Dhabi would be incomplete without trying the desert safari, walking along the waterfront Corniche, boat rides, shopping at the many malls, visiting the Ferrari World, etc. Whatever you’re looking for, from historic sacred sites to the finest dining and high-end shopping to touring the Arabian Desert, Abu Dhabi has it all and more.

itinerary.title: Day Trip to Abu Dhabi – Grand Mosque & Ferrari World
itinerary.text: After Breakfast. Drive to Abu Dhabi. Explore Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque Which is the central place of worship for citizens of the United Arab Emirates. This massive white structure is the largest mosque in the country, accommodating roughly 40,000 people. Inside you will find white marble columns with mother-of-pearl engravings, expansive Iranian carpets, and intricate crystal chandeliers. The Grand Mosque is one of the UAE’s most famous attractions. Things to Know Before You Go 1) The mosque is a must-see for first-time visitors to Abu Dhabi 2) Wear loose-fitting clothing that covers your legs and arms; women must wear a headscarf. 3) Don’t forget to bring sunglasses, as the white marble reflects sunlight. The first and largest of its kind in the world, this sprawling Ferrari-inspired theme park on the Yas Island is designed to provide an experience of lifetime. You can indulge in the fun and thrill with its more than 20 pulse-pounding rides and highlights, such as Formula Rosa, Fiorano GT Challenge, Scuderia Challenge, Paddock, V12 flume ride, Speed of Magic, BellItalia, and Galleria Ferrari. In the evening drive back to Dubai. Overnight Stay in Hotel

overview.text: Surrounded by the fierce Hajar Mountains, Ras Al Khaimah (or simply ‘RAK’, pronounced ‘rass-al-kai-muh’) is the UAE’s northernmost emirate. Both beach-sloths and outdoor enthusiasts love it here, thanks to sandy shores, sprawling oases and sun-baked desert, all on the emirate’s doorstep.While the call of the beach still laps up most visitors, who rarely move from the confines of their resort, RAK has been pulling out the stops in recent years to capitalise on its natural surroundings. Jebel Jais (the UAE’s tallest mountain) is front-and-centre of the development, offering the world’s longest zip line and a via ferrata route.After the swish resort beaches and adrenaline-fuelled mountain vistas, RAK City itself can seem bland. To see the city looking its best, head here at sunset to join families and joggers for the evening promenade down Al Qawasim Corniche, fronting the creek and overlooked by the pearly white Sheikh Zayed Mosque.

overview.text: Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), is a city of immense contrasts and significance on the global stage. Situated on the northeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, Abu Dhabi is renowned for its opulent luxury, cultural heritage, and modern development. At the heart of Abu Dhabi is the grandeur of Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, one of the world’s largest and most magnificent mosques, adorned with intricate Islamic architecture and featuring the world’s largest hand-knotted carpet. This architectural masterpiece is a symbol of the city’s deep-rooted cultural and religious values. Abu Dhabi’s transformation from a desert town into a modern metropolis has been nothing short of astonishing. The city’s skyline is studded with impressive skyscrapers, including the Etihad Towers and the iconic Capital Gate, which leans at an angle greater than the Leaning Tower of Pisa. These architectural wonders showcase the city’s commitment to innovation and modernity. The emirate’s wealth, primarily derived from its vast oil reserves, has allowed it to invest heavily in infrastructure, education, and healthcare. The result is a city with world-class amenities, top-notch healthcare facilities, and a robust education system, including renowned institutions like New York University Abu Dhabi. Culturally, Abu Dhabi is a melting pot, with a diverse population from all over the world calling it home. The city embraces cultural diversity and hosts events such as the Abu Dhabi Festival, which celebrates music, arts, and culture from around the globe. The Louvre Abu Dhabi, an art and civilization museum, is another testament to the city’s commitment to promoting culture and heritage. Abu Dhabi’s natural beauty is not to be overlooked. The city’s coastline is dotted with pristine beaches and islands, including Yas Island, home to the Yas Marina Circuit, where the Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix takes place. The nearby Ferrari World theme park and Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi provide entertainment options for all ages. One of Abu Dhabi’s most ambitious projects is Saadiyat Island, envisioned as a cultural and tourism hub with museums, art galleries, and luxurious resorts. The Guggenheim Abu Dhabi and the Zayed National Museum are among the cultural institutions set to grace this island in the coming years. overview.text: Dubai, often referred to as the “City of Gold” or the “Pearl of the Gulf,” is a captivating and dynamic metropolis located in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Nestled on the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, Dubai has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past few decades, evolving from a small fishing village into a global hub for finance, tourism, and innovation. One of Dubai’s most iconic features is its stunning skyline, dominated by awe-inspiring skyscrapers such as the Burj Khalifa, the world’s tallest building. This architectural marvel is a testament to Dubai’s ambition and commitment to pushing the boundaries of what is possible. It serves as a symbol of the city’s determination to be at the forefront of modernity and innovation. Dubai’s economic prosperity is underpinned by its strategic location as a major global business and transportation hub. The city’s state-of-the-art ports and airports facilitate trade and commerce, making it a vital link in the global supply chain. Additionally, Dubai has positioned itself as a tax-free haven, attracting businesses and investors from around the world. Tourism plays a significant role in Dubai’s economy, with millions of visitors flocking to the city each year. Dubai offers an array of attractions, from luxurious resorts and pristine beaches to world-class shopping and entertainment options. The Palm Jumeirah, an artificial island shaped like a palm tree, and the Dubai Mall, one of the largest shopping malls on the planet, are just a few of the must-see destinations. Dubai’s commitment to innovation and technology is evident in projects like the Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, which have fostered a thriving tech and media sector. Moreover, the city’s dedication to sustainability is reflected in initiatives like the Dubai Expo 2020, which showcased cutting-edge sustainable technologies and solutions to address global challenges. The cultural diversity in Dubai is a reflection of its open and inclusive society. The city is home to people from all corners of the world, creating a rich tapestry of cultures, languages, and traditions. Dubai’s commitment to tolerance and coexistence has made it a model for multiculturalism in the Middle East. Dubai also boasts a thriving arts and cultural scene, with world-class museums, galleries, and theaters. The Dubai Opera House, for example, hosts a wide range of international performances, from classical music to contemporary theater. In terms of lifestyle, Dubai offers an unparalleled blend of modernity and tradition. While it embraces all the conveniences of a cosmopolitan city, it also respects its heritage and traditions, evident in places like the historic Al Fahidi District and the bustling souks where traditional crafts and spices are sold. In conclusion, Dubai stands as a testament to human ambition and innovation. This city in the desert has defied the odds, transforming itself into a global powerhouse known for its striking architecture, economic prowess, and cultural vibrancy. It continues to be a place where dreams are turned into reality, attracting people from all walks of life who seek to be part of its incredible journey of growth and development.

overview.text: Sharjah is one of the seven emirates of the Gulf country the United Arab Emirates or UAE. It has also been awarded the title of the Cultural Capital of the Arab World in 1998 by UNESCO and again as the Capital of Islamic Culture in 2014. It is the third largest city in the UAE and one of the fastest growing cities in the world. Sharjah is a must visit for any lover of Islamic art and history as it boasts many world class museums. It is also a visual feast to walk around the inner city of Sharjah with its blend of traditional and modern Islamic architecture with many beautiful mosques dotting the entire city. The city is also a commercial centre and with the set up of its two major Free Trade Zones in recent years, Sharjah is witnessing massive foreign investment in the industrial sector. Sharjah is a landscaped city with many beautiful gardens, promenades and desert parks to enjoy on foot. The city is designed to represent to the world the perfect blend of traditional and contemporary style while keeping the tenets of Islam at its core. Sharjah is a ‘dry’ city, which means that consumption and sale of alcohol is prohibited without a liquor permit. It also has strict decency laws that require men and women, tourist or residents, to dress conservatively and appropriately.

overview.text: Surrounded by the fierce Hajar Mountains, Ras Al Khaimah (or simply ‘RAK’, pronounced ‘rass-al-kai-muh’) is the UAE’s northernmost emirate. overview.text: Dubai, often described as the “City of Gold” and the “Jewel of the Middle East,” is a dazzling metropolis that embodies luxury, innovation, and extravagance like no other place on Earth. Nestled along the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, this gleaming emirate has undergone a remarkable transformation over the decades, evolving from a modest desert town into a global icon of opulence and modernity. The most iconic symbol of Dubai’s ambition and grandeur is undoubtedly the Burj Khalifa, the world’s tallest skyscraper that seems to touch the very heavens. It pierces the skyline like a shimmering needle of glass and steel, symbolizing Dubai’s relentless pursuit of architectural excellence. The city’s skyline is a mesmerizing tapestry of gleaming towers, including the twisted Cayan Tower and the majestic Emirates Towers, creating a futuristic landscape that captures the imagination. Dubai’s economic prowess is underpinned by its strategic location as a hub for international trade and commerce. Its modern ports and world-class airports have positioned it as a crucial gateway for global business, while its free trade zones have enticed companies from all corners of the world to set up shop in this tax-free haven. Dubai’s visionary leadership has also led to the creation of Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), a thriving financial hub that rivals those of global financial giants. Tourism is at the heart of Dubai’s success story, with millions of visitors flocking to the city each year to experience its unparalleled luxury and entertainment. From the Palm Jumeirah, an artificial island that resembles a palm tree, to the extravagant Burj Al Arab, a seven-star hotel, Dubai boasts an array of world-class accommodations and attractions. The Dubai Mall, a shopping haven with its own indoor ice rink and aquarium, is a testament to the city’s dedication to offering unparalleled experiences. Dubai’s commitment to innovation and technology is evident in projects such as the Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, which have fostered a thriving tech and media sector. Moreover, the city’s dedication to sustainability is reflected in initiatives like the Dubai Expo 2020, a showcase of cutting-edge sustainable technologies and solutions to address global challenges. Culturally, Dubai is a dynamic blend of tradition and modernity. The city’s multicultural society welcomes people from all walks of life, creating a rich tapestry of languages, customs, and traditions. The historic Al Fahidi District and the bustling souks provide glimpses into the city’s rich heritage, while the Dubai Opera House hosts a diverse array of international performances, from classical music to contemporary theater. In conclusion, Dubai is a glittering oasis in the desert, a place where ambition knows no bounds, and where dreams are turned into reality. Its relentless pursuit of excellence, innovation, and luxury has elevated it to a status that few cities can match. With its iconic landmarks, economic prowess, and cultural vibrancy, Dubai continues to captivate the world’s imagination, attracting those who seek to experience the epitome of modernity and extravagance.

Glittering like a jewel of the desert, the glamorous city of Dubai is a land of dreams.
The western area of Dubai benefits from small stretches of sandy beaches, which have helped to catalyze the city’s tourism industry. Dubai’s rulers have sought to increase the city’s limited seafronts, and, in the absence of natural offshore islands, developers were encouraged to construct giant man-made islands off the coast of the city. Others include the “World” islands, a cluster of small islands positioned to resemble a world map when viewed from above. Ultramodern skyscrapers rising against an azure sky forms the gleaming skyline of this cosmopolitan city. As night cloaks Dubai, the city comes alive with twinkling lights adorning these tall superstructures. A drive along Downtown Dubai at night leaves you mesmerized by a fantasy land of lights and colours that surrounds you. Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world, will leave you open-mouthed in wonder. Fall under the spell of the largest dancing fountain in the world, the Dubai Fountain. Swim with the sharks in the gigantic aquarium at Dubai Mall and lose yourself to a world of make-believe at Mall of the Emirates. A curious blend of traditions and modernization can be seen in every corner of Dubai. A perfect example of this is Al Fahidi Fort, the oldest building in Dubai which is surrounded by a fast-paced metropolis. The sprawling Miracle Garden and Dubai Creek Park is a testament to the determination of the people of Dubai, to beat the odds and grow vibrant blooms smack in the middle of the desert.

overview.text: Chiang Mai (referred to as “the rose of the north”) is situated in Northern Thailand, 700km north of the capital city of Bangkok. Chiang Mai is the second largest city in Thailand, yet only has a population of around 200,000. Compare this to Bangkok which has about 9 million and it is easy to see why even the Thai people in Bangkok love to visit Chiang Mai for a holiday. The city is now becoming increasingly popular with overseas travellers as word spreads of this magnificent tourist location. There are various ways to travel to and visit Chiang Mai. From Bangkok it is a 1hr flight. In the last 25 or so years tourism has gradually transformed this once sleepy area into a travellers paradise whilst still maintaining its provincial charm. The ever-friendly and polite Thai people are full of smiles (Thailand = LOS = Land of Smiles). There are a million things to see and do, the food tastes sensational, it is a shopper’s paradise and a visit to Chiang Mai can even be done on a shoestring. Chiang Mai was built in 1296 as a walled city surrounded by a moat. The old city was roughly 1.5km square. Whilst a good portion of the original city wall has collapsed the four corner bastions are still intact along with various other sections. The original moat is still in use to this day. Chiang Mai city is basically made up now of the old city (within the walled area) and the new city which has grown up around it. Grab a Tuk-Tuk and go for a scenic visit to Chiang Mai’s lovely moat and the ancient walls of the old city. If you like ancient temples (Wats) and buildings, then visit Chiang Mai and the surrounding areas, they are full of them, several hundred in fact. A good number of these ancient temples are still in use today by the Buddhist monks.

Thailand’s northernmost province Chiang Rai is located 785 kilometers from Bangkok, and borders Myanmar to the north and Laos to the east. The province was built by Konh Mengrai in 1262, and is mainly very a mountainous terrain, forming the “Golden Triangle” around the Mekong river. Chiang Rai is an interesting place for tourists to visit on their trip to Thailand if they are eager to experience the area’s natural attractions, and learn about the place and Thailand’s past. An important reason for tourism in the area is the local hill tribes, and it is usually something tourists in this area want to experience. The hill tribes make their own goods such as jewelry, etc. which is very popular to buy. Additionally, the province has a number of important sights, including Mai Sai, Chiang Saen, which is home to many ancient ruins, and Doi Hua Mae Kham which is home to a number of tribal villages, all of which is worth experiencing on your trip to Thailand.

overview.place: Bangkok – the Capital City of Thailand

itinerary.title: Arrival at Chiangmai

itinerary.title: Chiang Mai City Tour
itinerary.text: After breakfast, Drive to the Mae Sa Elephant Camp to watch elephant activities like the elephants bathing. Here you have an option of riding the elephants. Elephants are considered as spiritual animals in Thailand. They are called God of Elephants. There are many elephant camps in Chiang Mai; Mae Sa is one of the largest one. They have more than seventy elephants that were trained from they were 2 or 3 years old. After lunch, we will proceed to the Sankampang area to see manufacture of Thai crafts. Sankampang is famous for its handicrafts and is the main production place of Thai Silk. Here we can see how Thai Silk is produced. Then drive for about 45 minutes up to the mountain and visit the magnificent Wat Phrathat Doi Suthep, which is the most important religious destination in this city. This Buddhist temple has a very colourful history and cannot be missed for a Chiang Mai tour. Overnight stay at the Hotel.

itinerary.title: Chiang Mai – Golden Triangle – Chiang Rai
itinerary.text: After Breakfast, we will drive up northward to the mountainous town Chiang Dao where we can have a stop and sample locally grown Royal Project coffee by a small lake. Proceed to Thaton where we will enjoy a lovely viewpoint from Thaton Temple. After lunch, continue to travel north for about 3 hours to the Golden Triangle via Doi Mae Salong. Opium poppy was used to be widely planted in the Mae Salong; but after it was prohibited by the government, they became tea plantation. Drive to the Golden Triangle and stay overnight at Chiang Rai. Overnight stay at the Hotel.

itinerary.title: Golden Triangle – Chiang Rai – Chiang Mai
itinerary.text: After Breakfast, we will transfer to Sop Ruak to see the point of the Golden Triangle where the Mekong River converges Laos, Myanmar and Thailand. Board a private speed boat to explore the bordered area along the Mekong River and step onto Laotian territory on Don Sao Island (Please bring your original passport for this activity). Disembark at the Chiang Saen old city and visit the ancient ruin and temples. After lunch, have a visit of the spectacular Wat Rong Khun before going back to Chiang Mai. The buildings in the temple are all handmade with white clays and pieces of glass, which glistening under the sun light. Reach Chiang Mai and stay overnight. Overnight stay at the Hotel / Resort

Visit the Golden Buddha Temple (Wat Traimit), Located at the end of the China Town’s Yaowarat Road, near Hualampong Railway Station, Wat Traimit houses the world’s largest massive gold seated Buddha measuring nearly five meters in height and weighing five and half tons. In the past, artisans crafted the buddhas in gold and disguised them from invading armies by a covering of stucco and plaster. Also pay a Visit to the Marble Temple (Wat Ben), Wat Benjamabhopit, most commonly called Wat Benja was built in by King Rama V in 1900 and is renowned for more than one reasons. Nickednamed ‘The Marble Temple’ for all the external walls of the main temple are covered with marble imported from Italy, but also for being the temple embossed on the back of 5-baht coins! Located near the many government offices and palaces, this wat is highly revered and is often visited by high ranked officials. Overnight stay at the Hotel

Trips to Pattaya often start from Bangkok which is about 1.5 hour drive from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport.Tourism in Pattaya flourished in the 1980s with the great development of hotels and resorts. Pattaya is now centre of many of the large and sophisticated international hotel chains and you will find a fine selection of high-class restaurants and the possibility of a more “quiet” night life. Phuket lies in the Andaman Sea on Thailand’s Indian Ocean coast located 867 kilometers south of Bangkok. Phuket is blessed with magnificent coves and bays, palm-filled, white beaches, small surrounding islands, hospitable people and great seafood. Also delightful Chinese-Portuguese architecture, numerous sporting and leisure opportunities, a lush tropical landscape – which helps to create a nice atmosphere for a truly memorable Thailand trip. The most famous beaches are Patong, Kata, Karon, Kamala and Nai Harn Beach. Phuket islands are ideal for sailing, diving, snorkeling, golfing and all kinds of sports and entertainment you could wish for. You can also take a trip with a submarine to discover the colorful marine life below the surface. There are plenty of accommodations, ranging from standard bungalows to 5-star hotels.
Phuket’s former wealth derived from tin and rubber, and enjoyed a rich and colorful history. The island was one of the main trade routes between India and China, and is frequently mentioned in foreign ship company logos. It is a very attractive island for sightseeing, with beautiful beaches and wooded hillsides. Its population of 1.6 million people ranks on place 6 among all provinces. Approximately 2.8 million square feet of the area is forest. The main industry today is rice cultivation. The average income per head is 14,343 Baht.
But in recent times, Phuket’s main income was tourism, which has transformed the island into Thailand’s wealthiest province. One might expect that the prices are a bit higher than on the mainland. Western Phuket was hit hard by the tsunami in the Indian Ocean in December 2004, but there is almost no evidence left on the damage.
Phuket is very popular as a tourist destination and most of the beaches on the west coast of Phuket town in the southeast and the airport in the north.

overview.text:
Phuket is Thailand’s largest island and is the size of Singapore, 48 km long and 21 km at the widest part. Phuket lies in the Andaman Sea on Thailand’s Indian Ocean coast located 867 kilometers south of Bangkok. Phuket is blessed with magnificent coves and bays, palm-filled, white beaches, small surrounding islands, hospitable people and great seafood. Also delightful Chinese-Portuguese architecture, numerous sporting and leisure opportunities, a lush tropical landscape – which helps to create a nice atmosphere for a truly memorable Thailand trip. The most famous beaches are Patong, Kata, Karon, Kamala and Nai Harn Beach. Phuket islands are ideal for sailing, diving, snorkeling, golfing and all kinds of sports and entertainment you could wish for. You can also take a trip with a submarine to discover the colorful marine life below the surface. There are plenty of accommodations, ranging from standard bungalows to 5-star hotels.
Phuket’s former wealth derived from tin and rubber, and enjoyed a rich and colorful history. The island was one of the main trade routes between India and China, and is frequently mentioned in foreign ship company logos. It is a very attractive island for sightseeing, with beautiful beaches and wooded hillsides. Its population of 1.6 million people ranks on place 6 among all provinces. Approximately 2.8 million square feet of the area is forest. The main industry today is rice cultivation. The average income per head is 14,343 Baht.
But in recent times, Phuket’s main income was tourism, which has transformed the island into Thailand’s wealthiest province. One might expect that the prices are a bit higher than on the mainland. Western Phuket was hit hard by the tsunami in the Indian Ocean in December 2004, but there is almost no evidence left on the damage.
Phuket is very popular as a tourist destination and most of the beaches on the west coast of Phuket town in the southeast and the airport in the north.

overview.text: Hua Hin is a seaside resort on the Gulf of Thailand, in the southern Thai province of Prachuap Khiri Khan. Once a quiet fishing village, it grew into a fashionable escape for residents of Bangkok after the 1920s, when the Thai royal family built summer palaces here. Hua Hin Beach, popular for kitesurfing and other water sports, is the main stretch of sand, lined with high-end hotels and seafood shacks.

overview.place: Bangkok – the Capital City of Thailand
overview.text: Bangkok, the capital city of Thailand, is a bustling and vibrant metropolis that seamlessly blends ancient traditions with modernity. Situated in the heart of Southeast Asia, along the banks of the Chao Phraya River, Bangkok is a city of contrasts, where towering skyscrapers stand beside historic temples, and street food stalls share the roads with luxury shopping malls. At the heart of Bangkok’s cultural and spiritual heritage lies the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha. These magnificent structures, adorned with intricate golden spires and intricate artwork, showcase the city’s deep-rooted reverence for Buddhism and its rich royal history. Beyond its historical sites, Bangkok is a city that never sleeps. The bustling streets of Khao San Road cater to backpackers and partygoers, while Sukhumvit Road offers upscale dining, shopping, and entertainment options. The vibrant street food scene is a culinary adventure in itself, with stalls serving up delicious Thai dishes on almost every corner. Bangkok is also a shopper’s paradise, from the sprawling Chatuchak Weekend Market to the upscale boutiques of Siam Paragon and CentralWorld. The city offers everything from traditional handicrafts to high-end fashion, making it a mecca for shopaholics. Despite its urban chaos, Bangkok also provides pockets of tranquility. Lumphini Park offers a serene escape from the city’s hustle and bustle, and the Chao Phraya River provides a picturesque backdrop for boat rides that offer a unique perspective of the city. In conclusion, Bangkok is a city of captivating contradictions, where ancient temples coexist with modern skyscrapers, and where traditional culture mingles with contemporary lifestyles. Its dynamic energy, rich cultural heritage, and diverse offerings make it an enchanting destination that leaves a lasting impression on all who visit.

The island was one of the main trade routes between India and China, and is frequently mentioned in foreign ship company logos. It is a very attractive island for sightseeing, with beautiful beaches and wooded hillsides. Its population of 1.6 million people ranks on place 6 among all provinces. Approximately 2.8 million square feet of the area is forest. The main industry today is rice cultivation. The average income per head is 14,343 Baht.
But in recent times, Phuket’s main income was tourism, which has transformed the island into Thailand’s wealthiest province. One might expect that the prices are a bit higher than on the mainland. Western Phuket was hit hard by the tsunami in the Indian Ocean in December 2004, but there is almost no evidence left on the damage.
Phuket is very popular as a tourist destination and most of the beaches on the west coast of Phuket town in the southeast and the airport in the north.

overview.text: Krabi – a province that embraces both the mainland and some idyllic islands – is characterised by unique limestone formations and lush vegetation. The limestone outcrops are a magnet for both rock climbers and camera crews shooting commercials, TV shows and films. Krabi Town is the main jump-off point for travellers en route to the beaches and islands of Krabi Province. Those venturing north of Krabi Town into the interior will find a shrine, a hot springs waterfall and a wildlife sanctuary.

overview.heading: Town
overview.text: Thanon Maharat hosts the main market and most restaurants and shops, while there are guesthouses and hotels on Thanon Chao Fa, just a few minutes’ walk from Chao Fa Pier. There are boats for hire at the pier to mangroves on the opposite bank of the Krabi River, whre a small fishing community lives in wooden huts on stilts. The trips include two 100m (328ft) limestone pinnacles that rise beside the river, called Khao Khanab Nam. One peak has a series of caves with impressive stalactites and stalagmites.

overview.heading: Krabi Interior
overview.text: Set into forests and cliffs, 9km (6 miles) north of Krabi Town, Wat Tham Seua has 1,272 steps leading to a 600m (1,970ft) peak. It has fantastic views and a small shrine with a Buddha footprint in the rock. Southeast of Krabi Town is Hot Springs Waterfall, where people first bathe in the hot water as it cascades down the boulders, before dipping into a cool stream. A 10-minute drive east of the waterfall, the Khao Nor Chu Chi Wildlife Sanctuary is said to be the last patch of lowland rainforest in Thailand. It’s also one of the few habitats of an endangered bird called Gurneys Pitta.

overview.heading: Best Beaches
overview.text: Three Krabi beaches are accessible by road: Hat Khlong Muang, Hat Noppharat Thara and Ao Nang, but most visitors head to one of the outlying beaches for which Krabi is most famous. Most boats go to Hat Railay West, on the western side of the peninsula, where the absence of a pier means a short wade to shore. On the opposite side of the peninsula Hat Railay East, which is backed by dense mangroves, is less scenic and not great for swimming. Accordingly, the bungalows here are lower priced, but get their fair share of trade, as there’s only a 5-minute walk from one beach to the other. The same people appreciating sunsets on Railay West are often seen a few hours later enjoying fire juggling and all-night parties at Railay East.The prettiest beach, Hat Tham Phra Nang, has a single accommodation option, Rayavadee Resort. Day-trippers flock here from Railay West and Railay East to sunbathe, swim and snorkel.The beach Hat Ton Sai is popular with budget travellers for its cheaper accommodation and vibrant nightlife. Beach bars are open until the early hours and host monthly full-moon parties. The sea view is beautiful, but the sand is less white, and at low tide gets muddy.

overview.heading: Rock Climbing
overview.text: Most of Krabi’s 600-plus climbing routes are located on Railay Bay peninsula, which has dramatic sheer limestone cliffs facing the sea. The climbs involve crags, steep pocketed walls, overhangs and hanging stalactites, and are suitable for beginners through to professionals. Among the most popular is the phenomenal, and challenging, Thaiwand Wall at the southern end. Any of the Railay climbing operators will advise on the best routes, some of which are accessed by a combination of boat and jungle hike.

overview.text: Chiang Mai (referred to as “the rose of the north”) is situated in Northern Thailand, 700km north of the capital city of Bangkok. Chiang Mai is the second largest city in Thailand, yet only has a population of around 200,000. Compare this to Bangkok which has about 9 million and it is easy to see why even the Thai people in Bangkok love to visit Chiang Mai for a holiday. The city is now becoming increasingly popular with overseas travellers as word spreads of this magnificent tourist location. There are various ways to travel to and visit Chiang Mai. From Bangkok it is a 1hr flight. In the last 25 or so years tourism has gradually transformed this once sleepy area into a travellers paradise whilst still maintaining its provincial charm. The ever-friendly and polite Thai people are full of smiles (Thailand = LOS = Land of Smiles). There are a million things to see and do, the food tastes sensational, it is a shopper’s paradise and a visit to Chiang Mai can even be done on a shoestring. Chiang Mai was built in 1296 as a walled city surrounded by a moat. The old city was roughly 1.5km square. Whilst a good portion of the original city wall has collapsed the four corner bastions are still intact along with various other sections. The original moat is still in use to this day. Chiang Mai city is basically made up now of the old city (within the walled area) and the new city which has grown up around it. Grab a Tuk-Tuk and go for a scenic visit to Chiang Mai’s lovely moat and the ancient walls of the old city. If you like ancient temples (Wats) and buildings, then visit Chiang Mai and the surrounding areas, they are full of them, several hundred in fact. A good number of these ancient temples are still in use today by the Buddhist monks.
